Container.Name: PlayheadTV
Container.Overview: Your own linear TV channels assembled on the client: the backend owns the schedule and the sync, the player stitches programs, bumpers and commercials from your Jellyfin library. No server-side transcoding, no tuner.
Container.Changes: Dropped the legacy Networking/Data/Environment blocks (the two env vars are already defaults in the image). They duplicate the Config entries and broke a recreate on 17/nov. Initial template. Backend v0.3.15, pinned: this project publishes no latest tag.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: linear tv channels schedule epg jellyfin virtual channels nostalgia quasitv ersatztv tunarr streaming
Container.Description:
Playhead TV gives you linear TV again: a channel with a schedule that keeps playing whether you watch it or not. The difference from ErsatzTV and Tunarr is where the work happens. Their server runs ffmpeg to package one continuous stream per channel. Playhead TV keeps that work on the client: each client talks to Jellyfin, resolves the schedule from this backend, and plays the original files itself, stitching programs, commercials and bumpers with its own preload and crossfade logic. The backend only owns scheduling metadata and user/device sync, and never touches video.
### What this container is
This is the **backend**: REST API, MCP endpoint and the admin web UI. It is not the player. The players are separate Flutter apps (Linux and Windows desktop, Android TV, Android phones; iOS and tvOS still ahead), published as `client-vX.Y.Z` releases in the project. Install this first, then point the client at it.
A Jellyfin server is the media source. Playhead TV does not hold a library of its own.
### First start: create the admin user before you expose the port
A fresh instance has no user, and the endpoint that creates the first one is public until it is used. From a terminal, before anyone else can reach the port:
``` curl -sS -X POST http://<server>:9394/app-users \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"email": "you@example.com", "password": "a strong password"}' ```
The password must be at least 8 characters. Then open `/admin/` and sign in. After the first user exists the endpoint answers 409, so it cannot be used again.
### Backups
`/data` holds `playheadtv.db` and `encryption.key`. Stored media-source credentials are encrypted with that key, which is generated on first start if you do not set `PLAYHEADTV_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. Back up both together: a backup of the database without the key cannot decrypt the credentials.
### Container notes
- **No `latest` tag exists.** The template pins `v0.3.15` on purpose, matching the project rule of pinning an immutable release. To upgrade, change the repository tag after reading the release notes. - The image has no shell and no curl. The healthcheck calls the server binary itself (`/server healthcheck`), already set in the extra parameters. - The image runs as root by default. The template adds `--user 99:100` so `/data` stays `nobody:users` like every other Unraid container. - The admin UI is served on the same port as the API (9394). Put a TLS reverse proxy in front if it needs to be reachable from outside your LAN. - `PLAYHEADTV_EPG_WINDOW` (default 72h) is how far ahead the guide is materialized. Clients cache that window, so a longer window means more offline autonomy and more data.
Project documentation: https://github.com/rafaelvieiras/playheadtv

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTP port for the REST API, the MCP endpoint and the admin UI at /admin/.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Database and encryption key. Back up both together: the key decrypts the stored credentials.

Config.Name: EPG window
Config.Description: How far ahead the guide is materialized, between 1h and 720h. Clients can play offline for about as long.

Config.Name: Log level
Config.Description: error, warn, info, debug or trace. Empty keeps the default output.

Config.Name: Encryption key
Config.Description: 32 random bytes, base64 (openssl rand -base64 32). Empty: generated into /data/encryption.key on first start.
